mike: quick follow-up to the span-slimming discussion — wanted to call out a few real-world cases that could wreck cost attribution if we don't handle them.
jamie: sure, what popped up?
sarah: is this about attributes that only show up on deep DB/HTTP spans?
mike: yes. some tenants only stamp billing info on an intermediate span (eg db.query) and if we prune that span we lose the billing_key entirely.
alex: hmm. we could require a tiny immutable envelope on the root containing the attribution keys we care about (billing_key, tier, cohort). keep that root envelope even when trimming children.
jamie: envelope on root seems safe, but requires agent/SDK changes. adoption will be gradual.
carmen: for backwards compatibility: accept a hashed_ref on older agents. ingest can attempt a late lookup to resolve hash -> billing_key.
mike: hashing avoids storing full keys everywhere which helps size & PII concerns. downside: extra lookup/caching complexity in ingest.
alex: suggestion: have agents stamp two things: joinpoint (on root) + hashed_refs on network-origin spans. Ingest uses joinpoint when present, otherwise does hash lookup triggered by hashed_ref.
sarah: and if the lookup fails we mark the trace as unattributed and surface it in a migration dashboard.
infra-bot: deploy: canary for obsv-agent v0.21 started at 2025-06-15T14:00Z targeting 5% edge fleet :rocket:
jamie: what does the joinpoint envelope shape look like? can we write a minimal snippet here?
mike: example envelope (kept brief):

```
joinpoint: billing_key=acct:acme-123, billing_hash=h1:9f3a..., cohort=cohort-v2, sdk=obsv-go@0.21
```

keep full billing_key only on root; leaf spans carry billing_hash when needed.
carmen: rollout plan idea: 1) require joinpoint for new SDKs; 2) accept hashed_ref from old SDKs and perform late-enrich; 3) treat unresolved hashes as "unattributed" but track metrics.
jamie: good. ingest implementation note: we should provide a bounded lookup budget and a fallback queue for async resolution. we also need a bloom filter to reduce wasted lookups.
alex: rough implementation estimate: cache+index + bloom filter + async worker, say 2-3 eng-weeks to get to a safe canary path.
mike: action items: jamie write a short RFC for the enrichment shim + envelope spec; alex to prototype cache & perf numbers; carmen to draft canary gating + dashboard metrics.
carmen: i'll add dashboard panels: percent traces with joinpoint present / hashed_only / missing. that'll be our migration signal.
sarah: one more thought — make the joinpoint versioned (eg joinpoint_v=1) so future schema changes are easier to migrate.
jamie: agreed. also add a header in ingest manifest to allow queries to join on either billing_key or billing_hash for a rolling window.
infra-bot: note: tracing-telemetry pipeline has a late-lookup quota configured for canary (100k/day). monitor alerts enabled.
alex: i'll run perf tests against 1M sample traces and post numbers by EOD Tuesday.
mike: thanks everyone — i'll fold this into a follow-up RFC draft and ping reviewers. :thumbsup!
